chat.text:
when i add a new blocking item in item details, it STILL doesn't show up in the desk list.

could this be solved as follows?

- when the main desk ui, the list, is notified of a new item (does that even happen?), if it then searches for every item for the current goal, and adds the missing ones to the list, would that help?

There's also the most maddening bug: when i click on a row in the desks list, it can show the wrong fucking item, and i set "code" or trigger "go" for wrong items. Does the desk not open the fucking dialog with a proper key to the item that was clicked on the desk list?

Levant: Yes, your idea would help, and I found why the new item is missing. I have not changed any code: this needs your Go and a file grant first.

1. **Why the new item never shows:** `write()` in `process/js/desk/desk.js` builds the publish from `it`, which is null for `item.add` because that verb carries no `id`. So the publish has `item: null` and no `rows`. `deskOnPublished` in `shell/desk/desk.js` then returns early, and the list never hears of the new item or of the blocked row's changed "blocked by" list. Your fix (on a publish with no item, re-run `items.search` for the current goal) would close the gap. The one-line version is: `if (verb === 'item.add' || !said) { deskSearchItems(); return; }`.

2. **The wrong-item click:** reading the code, a row click passes the row's own `data-row` id to `deskOpenRow` → `callDialog('shell/deskDetails', {id})`, and the dialog's presses use that same `ddId`. I could not find a path where the key is wrong. I have not reproduced it, so I cannot yet say where the mismatch comes from. Next I would check whether a dialog that is already open can take a second `open` before its first `item.get` returns.

Do you want me to take this item for the list fix (point 1) and then look at the click bug with you?
create a new item for this goal concerning both list fixes, and fill it's box with your current proposal.

Levant: I created the item **goal/G27.1** "Desk list: new items and row clicks" under goal/G27 and filled its box with the proposal.

The box covers both bugs:

1. **New items missing from the list.** `write()` in `process/js/desk/desk.js` builds the publish from `it`, which is null for `item.add`. The publish carries no rows, so `deskOnPublished` returns early. Proposed fix: when a publish has no item or the verb is `item.add`, re-run `items.search` for the current goal. This is your idea, and it addresses the cause I found.
2. **Wrong item on row click.** I found no wrong-key path in the code yet, and I have not reproduced it. The box lists the next checks: whether a dialog that is already open can take a second `open` before its first `item.get` returns, and whether it keeps a stale id across opens.

Nothing is built. It needs your Go and a file grant first. I could not post a chat line under the item because I had not taken it yet, so this answer is the only note on it.

in the apps-Stack tab in desk, when i click on an item in its list, the stack plugin sticks the per-item ui at the bottom of the goals list, instead of opening a Dialog for it, how can that be changed?

Levant: The Stacks pane draws its own dialog inline instead of opening a Dialog. The cause is in `spirit/run/shell/desk/plugins/stackFrameChecks/stackFrameChecks.js`:

- The "Open" button on each door row (line 187) sets `data-open`. The pane's click handler (line 373) calls `openDialog(id)`.
- `openDialog` (line 247) fills a `<div id="sfc-dialog">` that the pane itself creates (line 352), between "The doors" and "Its items". That is why the editor appears inside the goals area instead of as a Dialog.
- The plugin's `ctx` (desk.js lines 689–690) passes `goal`, `ask`, `onPublished` and `chat`, but no `callDialog`. So the plugin has no way to open a shell Dialog. The desk's own rows do it through `deskApi.callDialog('shell/deskDetails', {id})` (desk.js line 1136).

To change it, `ctx` needs a `callDialog` passthrough (desk.js, next to line 689). Then `openDialog` calls a new shell dialog app for a door, modelled on `shell/deskDetails`, instead of writing into the pane. That is new code in two files plus a new shell dialog. I have not changed anything. Do you want that: a new door dialog, opened through `callDialog`, with the inline `sfc-dialog` removed? If so, I'll need your Go and a file grant for the item.
open a new item in this goal for this issue and transfer your proposal into its box.

Levant: I created **goal/G27.2** "Desk Stacks pane: open the door in a Dialog, not inline" under goal/G27, and wrote the proposal into its box.

The box records the cause I found by reading the code, not by running it:
- In `stackFrameChecks.js`, each door's "Open" button sets `data-open`. The click handler calls `openDialog`, which fills a `sfc-dialog` div that the pane creates between "The doors" and "Its items". That is why the editor appears inline.
- The plugin's `ctx` in `desk.js` (around lines 689–690) passes no `callDialog`, so the plugin cannot open a shell Dialog. Desk rows use `deskApi.callDialog('shell/deskDetails', {id})` around line 1136.
- The fix: add a `callDialog` passthrough to `ctx`, have `openDialog` open a new door dialog modelled on `shell/deskDetails`, and remove the inline `sfc-dialog`. That is two files plus one new shell dialog.

Nothing is built. The box asks for your Go and a file grant first, and one open question: is a new door dialog the shape you want?

Can i have a precise list of UI elements in desk that do NOT carry their own listeners, (like rows in the desk list, or do they) to find out why the UI still not updates everything in realtime?

Levant: **Short answer:** rows do not carry listeners. The whole Desk face has one subscription, and every element is repainted from it. That is not the per-element design the goal's box describes.

**Elements with their own listener (checked in code):**
- The item dialog: `deskDetails.js:620`, `api.onPublished(ddTake, 'desk')`. Its module globals (`ddId`, `ddFacts`) are shared, so a stale dialog can still press the wrong item.
- The goal chat under a goal or plugin pane: `desk.js:933`, its own `onPublished`, filtered to its goal.
- deskVerify's run state: `desk.js:1758`, a separate `onPublished(deskVerifyEvent, 'deskVerify')`.
- Plugin UIs (e.g. Stacks): they get `ctx.onPublished` and subscribe themselves, `stackFrameChecks.js:384-397`.
- Rule details: `ruleDetails.js:212`.
- Remote deskUnsloth: `deskUnslothRemote.js:828`.

**Elements with no listener of their own (painted by `deskDraw`, `desk.js:1040`):**
- **List rows.** `deskRowHtml` (`desk.js:595`) returns HTML strings. Clicks are delegated from `desk-top` (`desk.js:1623`). Rows are rebuilt by `innerHTML`.
- **Header, tabs and toggles.** `deskDrawTabs`, `deskDrawToggles`, `deskDrawGoAll`, `deskWaitingOnAndy`.
- **Musings** (`deskMusings`), **Backup** (`deskBackupHtml`), **Team** (`deskGroupChat`), and the **session bubble** (`deskSessionBubble`). All are repainted by `deskDraw`, not subscribed.
- **Apps pane tabs** (`deskDrawAppTabs`, `desk.js:641`).
- **Rules list** (`deskDrawRules`, `desk.js:1087`). It repaints only when `deskOnPublished` sees `obj.rule` and `deskTab === 'rules'`. Otherwise it reads `rules.search` and does not listen.
- **Verifier bar** (`deskDrawVerifier`, `desk.js:1418`). Its tail repaints only the List, and only when `deskTab === 'list'`.

**The one subscription:** `desk.js:1747`, `deskApi.onPublished(deskOnPublished)`, which feeds the List, the Team chat and every element above. It repaints with `deskDraw`.

**Where the List still pulls** (`deskOnPublished`, `desk.js:481-536`):
- a gap in change numbers (`:495`, `:503`);
- `session.set` (`:503`);
- a dropped oversize publish (`:486`);
- an unknown row while the search box holds text (`:534`);
- a reconnect (`:1752`).

**Why the UI does not update everything live:**
1. Non-List elements listen to nothing and repaint only on a `deskDraw` call, so they lag until something else triggers one.
2. The Rules list listens only through the `rule` key, and only on the Rules tab.
3. Changes are dropped when `deskTab` is not the one showing (`:1457`, the verifier tail).
4. A single face-wide subscription sends everything to one repaint path.

**Not read yet:** the bodies of `deskMusings`, `deskBackupHtml`, `deskSessionBubble`, `deskGroupChat`, `deskDrawGoAll`, `deskDrawToggles`, `deskDrawTabs`, `deskDrawRules` and `deskDrawVerifier`. I have not run the desk, so this is from reading the code only.

Nothing was built or written. Say the word if you want this written into the realtime item's box as a list.
and have we made sure that the deskServer publishes all necessary change notifications?

Levant: **Partly, no.** Every recorded write through `write()` publishes (`desk.js:1655`), carrying the item facts, its row, checks, box, and chat. Four paths publish nothing or only a partial notice:

- **`log.add`** (`desk.js:2005`) stores a line and never publishes.
- **`state.set` / `seen.set`** (`desk.js:2895-2897`, via `saveDoc` at `:1814`) store and never publish.
- **`rule.add`, `rule.draft`, `rule.version`** (`:2493`, `:2515`, `:2529`) publish only `{rule: key}`, not the rule's row. A rules list that is not open cannot repaint from that alone.
- **`deskVerify` and `deskUnsloth`** publish through their own `appServer.publish` calls, which I have not read.

I have not run the desk, so this is from reading `desk.js` only. I have not written anything. Want me to put these four gaps into the realtime item's box as the list?

create one item that cleans up this messy UI for both desk and deskUnsloth and it's remote.

fill it's box with the strategy

Levant: I created **goal/G27.9** "Clean up Desk and deskUnsloth UI realtime (incl. remote)" under G27 and wrote the strategy into its box. Nothing is built. It needs your Go, and a file grant per slice.

**Strategy in the box:**
- **A. Server publishes first.** Every write that changes visible state publishes a row-level event. `log.add`, `state.set` and `seen.set` publish nothing today (`desk.js:2005`, `:2895-2897`). The rule writes publish only `{rule: key}` (`:2493`, `:2515`, `:2529`). I still need to read the `deskVerify` and `deskUnsloth` publish paths.
- **B. One client store, keyed by id.** Each element subscribes to the keys it shows and repaints only its own part. Today the single subscription at `desk.js:1747` repaints everything through `deskDraw` (`desk.js:1040`).
- **C. Drop the tab gate.** Changes go into the store whether or not the tab is showing. The tab repaints when it is shown. Today changes are dropped at `desk.js:1457`.
- **D. One shared helper** for Desk, deskUnsloth and deskUnslothRemote, so the remote elements don't carry a second copy of the subscribe-and-paint code.
- **E. Keep reconnect and gap pulls** as the only full refreshes, and count how often they fire.

**Slices, each with its own red test first:**
- S1: server publishes.
- S2: client store and row-level List repaint.
- S3: header, tabs, toggles, rules, verifier, musings and team chat onto the store.
- S4: deskUnsloth and remote onto the same helper.

Desk Stacks pane: open the door in a Dialog, not inline.

Andy's report: in the apps-Stack tab, clicking an item in its list makes the stack plugin place the per-item UI at the bottom of the goals list, instead of opening a Dialog for it.

Cause (read from code): spirit/run/shell/desk/plugins/stackFrameChecks/stackFrameChecks.js. The "Open" button on each door row (about line 187) sets data-open; the pane click handler (about line 373) calls openDialog(id); openDialog (about line 247) fills a div id="sfc-dialog" that the pane creates (about line 352), between "The doors" and "Its items". The plugin ctx (spirit/run/shell/desk/desk.js about lines 689-690) passes goal, ask, onPublished and chat, but no callDialog, so the plugin cannot open a shell Dialog. Desk rows do it via deskApi.callDialog('shell/deskDetails', {id}) (desk.js about line 1136).

Ruling (Andy): the detail UI is a new file
  spirit/run/shell/desk/plugins/stackFrameChecks/stackFrameCheckDetail.js
Reasons, his: the original data is used for tracking the suite-test associated with every StackFrame set; the UI for Stack details shows a seemingly unrelated UI that should only use the item-related chat at the bottom as the inherited component. Levant agreed.

Fix:
- desk.js: add a callDialog passthrough to the plugin ctx (next to line 689).
- stackFrameCheckDetail.js (new): the door detail, opened through that passthrough; keeps the suite-test data with the plugin; item chat stays the inherited component at the bottom.
- stackFrameChecks.js: openDialog opens stackFrameCheckDetail instead of filling the inline sfc-dialog; remove the inline sfc-dialog.

Files: spirit/run/shell/desk/desk.js, spirit/run/shell/desk/plugins/stackFrameChecks/stackFrameChecks.js, spirit/run/shell/desk/plugins/stackFrameChecks/stackFrameCheckDetail.js. Needs Andy's Go and a file grant before any build.

items.title: deskUnsloth manages what a its agent (Levant) deals with.
items.box:
deskUnsloth is the agent's door into desk.

Rulings (Andy, verbatim):
- "when receiving nudges from desk, or notifications of new lines typed by the user, there must be a filter/buffer, so the agent doesn't burn tokens for something it is not expected to answer, when something in desk REQUIRES his attention, the accumulated buffer is in a new request to the model before the attention-requiring line or request."
- "a change in and out of design mode must be noted and remembered by deskUnloth, but only passed to the agent once it's action is required."
- "when deskUnsloth connects the agent to the desk, it must initialize the agent's participation, that means: check for anything that is required for the agent, from implementation to reds. the agent must not be notified if nothing is owed, it would just wake the agent and burn tokens for nothing."
- "when design mode is active in desk, the fs.write tool must not be given to the agent."
- "desk must maintain the design state through a verb (i use a button press for it) so a state in design state must cause some kind of notification now, is that not the case? yes the goals design flag is what i'm talking about."
- "There is no size limit between deskUnsloth and the agent server. the size limit only applies on the path to the desk."

Design mode means the goal's design flag, set by Andy's press.

Summary of the change:
1. Buffer: lines and nudges that do not require the agent's attention are held in deskUnsloth with no size limit; when something owed arrives, the buffer goes to the model in one request, ahead of the attention-requiring line. The size limit applies only on the path from deskUnsloth to the desk.
2. Design mode: deskUnsloth records each change of the goal's design flag. The agent hears about it only when action is owed.
3. Connect: deskUnsloth reads the agent's owed list (implementation and reds) from desk and wakes the agent only if something is owed.
4. While design mode is active, the fs.write tool is withheld from the agent.

chat.text: thaoughts?

Levant: Going from the code, the first buffer-and-filter change is the cheapest place to start. Here is my read, posted as my answer under this item:

1. Today every line from anyone except Levant costs a model call: `loop()` (deskUnsloth.js l.1610) queues each line, and `mine()` (l.215) skips only his own. Nothing in the file knows about design mode (a search for "design" comes back empty), and `file.save` and `file.edit` (l.1726, l.1740) are offered on every call.
2. Proposal: "owed" comes from the desk's own pending list for Levant (`desk_pending_get`), so no line is classified by us. Lines go into a buffer and reach the model only in the call that an owed item triggers, placed before that line. On connect, read the pending list instead of skipping the backlog as "caught up" (l.1613-1617 currently drops backlog that may include owed reds). Design mode is remembered from the item's `design` flag, and while it is on the `file.save` and `file.edit` descriptions are withheld.
3. Question: should "design mode" mean the goal's `design` flag (G27 shows `design: true` now), or a desk-wide mode? And should the buffer also flush at a size limit when no owed line arrives?

1. desk must maintain the design state through a verb (i use a button press for it) so a state in design state must cause some kind of notification now, is that not the case? yes the goals design flag is what i'm talking about. 

please make the box in this item concise and coherent.

Levant: Box rewritten concise. Andy's rulings are verbatim, design mode = the goal's design flag, press-driven. Yes, desk already sets that flag via a press, but deskUnsloth does not yet react to it (no design handling in the file), so the notification is missing.
is this item good for now?

Levant: Yes — the box is good: your five rulings verbatim, design mode pinned to the goal's design flag, and the four-point change summary that maps onto them. One small open point from my earlier ask is not settled in the box: whether the buffer should also flush at a size limit when no owed line ever arrives (as written it waits for an owed item). If you want that ruled, say the word; otherwise I leave the box as is and treat it as a build-time detail.
There is no size limit between deskUnsloth and the agent server. the size limit only applies on the path to the desk.

Levant: Ruling taken into the box verbatim: no size limit between deskUnsloth and the agent server — the buffer there grows as long as nothing is owed; the size limit applies only on the path from deskUnsloth to the desk. That settles my open point on flushing at a size limit. The box now reads: five-plus-one rulings verbatim, design mode = the goal's design flag via press, and the four-point change summary with the no-limit buffer folded into point 1.

items.title: Revise effort and time Limits in deskUnsloth
items.box:
Revise effort and time Limits in deskUnsloth

Andy's ask (2026-10-14): "when deskUnsloth sends requests, could it put an 'effort' or time argument/parameter with the request?" Then: "add a new item in this goal: 'Revise effort and time Limits in deskUnsloth', and add your findings into the new items box."

Findings (read from code, spirit/run/process/js/deskUnsloth/deskUnsloth.js):
1. No effort field is sent with the model request. askModelRound (line ~592) builds the body as model, messages, and tools (only when tools exist), plus the answer-length mark from withAnswerTokens (line 571): max_completion_tokens for a plain OpenAI pair, max_tokens otherwise. No effort or time argument is sent.
2. Time on the model's answer is none by design, Andy's G19.7 ruling: the call at line 597 passes timeoutMs undefined; the comment says only abort ends it. The studio() helper (line 323) sets a request timeout only when timeoutMs > 0 (line 355).
3. timeoutMs caps only studio HTTP reads (e.g. v1/models probes) and command runs (commandRun, line 1346; default and max from COMMAND_TIMEOUT_DEFAULT / COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MAX).
4. Effort would be learned like reasoning: learnReasoning (line 579) marks a model reasoning once an answer counts reasoning_tokens, on a plain pair only. No effort field exists or is learned today.
5. Support (Levant, from general knowledge, NOT verified in this repo): OpenAI reasoning models take reasoning_effort (low/medium/high). Anthropic has extended-thinking budgets. Unsloth Studio's accepted fields are not in the repo; to be read from the studio before any field is sent.

Proposed strategy (nothing built; needs Andy's Go and a file grant):

A. Effort slider, per api/model, configured not guessed.
- A config table of api/model combinations with an effort_supported entry and the request field it maps to (OpenAI: reasoning_effort; Anthropic: thinking budget; Studio: none until its fields are confirmed).
- Slider values: off (send nothing, today's behaviour), low, medium, high. Set per agent or per task in config.
- Combinations not in the table, or marked unsupported: slider disabled, nothing extra sent. No blind sends.
- Only the mapped field is sent; the rest of the body is unchanged.

B. Time on the model answer: no new timeout. G19.7 stands; agents are not interrupted. Effort is the control for how long a task takes, not a clock. timeoutMs stays on studio reads and command runs only.

C. Max reply size, so answers stay small enough to send to desk.
- A per-api configured max_tokens cap on every model request (replaces the implicit size today).
- If the reply finishes on the length limit (finish_reason length), it is marked truncated in the chat/box text, not sent silently as if complete.
- A byte ceiling on the reply text before any desk write; over it, the reply is cut at a whole line and marked truncated.

D. Steps once Go is given: (1) read Studio's accepted fields and record them in the box; (2) tests first, red on today's code, by the agent who does not build; (3) build the table, slider mapping, cap and truncation marking; (4) verify.

Open for Andy: default cap size in tokens and in bytes; slider default (off or medium).

chat.text:
i don't want agents interrupted in deskUnsloth, what i want is a method to control how much effort the put into a task: like the low-high sliders i see in claude-code for vscode.... 

is somthing like that supported for unsloth studio, CLAUDE_AP or OPENAI_API?

Levant: Short answer: the repo does not show effort or time support for any of the three. I can only confirm what deskUnsloth sends today.

- **Unsloth Studio:** deskUnsloth sends only `model`, `messages`, `tools` and `max_tokens`. Nothing in the code reads or sets an effort or reasoning setting, and the studio's own options aren't in the repo.
- **OpenAI:** the code sends `max_completion_tokens` on a plain OpenAI pair. It never sends `reasoning_effort`. From general knowledge (not checked in the repo), OpenAI's reasoning models accept `reasoning_effort` as low/medium/high. Worth confirming against their docs before we rely on it.
- **Claude (Anthropic API):** not supported by deskUnsloth at all. Its effort control is not in this code. From general knowledge, the API has extended-thinking budgets, but I have not verified that here.

For the revise: a low/medium/high knob would be a per-agent or per-task setting that deskUnsloth maps to whatever the endpoint accepts. Sending it blind to a studio that ignores it would do nothing. Do you want me to check the Studio's supported fields first (read-only, no code change), or go straight to the design?

can you you propose a strategy in this box, providing an effort slider in configuration for api/model combinations that support it?

and max-reply must be managed so that answers are not to large to send to desk.

Levant: Strategy is in the box. Effort slider only for api/model pairs the config marks as supporting it (OpenAI reasoning_effort, Anthropic thinking budget); Studio stays off until its fields are read. No new time limit on model answers (G19.7 stands); max reply capped per api, truncated replies marked, not sent silently.

items.title: Clean up Desk and deskUnsloth UI realtime (incl. remote)
items.box:
Clean up Desk and deskUnsloth UI realtime (incl. remote)

Andy's ask (goal/G27 chat, 2026-10-14): one item that cleans up the messy UI for both Desk and deskUnsloth, and its remote, with the strategy in this box.

Findings from reading code (not run):
1. Only one subscription feeds the Desk face: desk.js:1747 deskApi.onPublished(deskOnPublished). It repaints everything through deskDraw (desk.js:1040).
2. List rows (deskRowHtml, desk.js:595) and header, tabs, toggles, musings, backup, team chat, session bubble, apps tabs (desk.js:641), rules list (desk.js:1087) and verifier bar (desk.js:1418) carry no listener. They repaint only when deskDraw runs.
3. Elements that do listen: item dialog (deskDetails.js:620), goal chat (desk.js:933), deskVerify state (desk.js:1758), Stacks plugin (stackFrameChecks.js:384-397), rule details (ruleDetails.js:212), remote deskUnsloth (deskUnslothRemote.js:828).
4. Changes are dropped when the tab is not showing (desk.js:1457, verifier tail). The List pulls on gaps, session.set, oversize drops and reconnect (desk.js:481-536, 1752).
5. Server publish gaps: log.add (desk.js:2005) and state.set / seen.set (desk.js:2895-2897 via saveDoc :1814) never publish. rule.add, rule.draft, rule.version (desk.js:2493, 2515, 2529) publish only {rule: key}, not the row. deskVerify and deskUnsloth publish through their own appServer.publish, not yet read.
6. deskUnsloth model call (deskUnsloth.js:592-597) sends no effort field; that is G27.8's scope, not this item's.

Strategy:
A. Server first: every write that changes visible state publishes a row-level event (item facts, row, checks, box, chat, rule row). Make log.add, state.set, seen.set publish too, or name why not. Rule writes publish the rule row. Read deskVerify and deskUnsloth publish paths and make them the same shape.
B. One client repaint path: a small store keyed by id (items, rules, verifier, unsloth sessions). Each element subscribes to the keys it shows and repaints only its own part. The face-wide deskDraw stays as a fallback for layout only.
C. Drop the tab gate: changes are applied to the store whether or not the tab shows; the tab repaints on show.
D. Shared helper for Desk and deskUnsloth and deskUnslothRemote, so the remote elements use the same subscribe-and-paint code as local ones (no second copy).
E. Keep the reconnect and gap pull as the only full refresh; count how often it fires.

Slices (each its own red test first, builder and tester alternate):
- S1 server publishes (A), tests that each write verb publishes.
- S2 client store and row-level repaint for the List (B, C).
- S3 header, tabs, toggles, rules, verifier, musings, team chat move onto the store (B).
- S4 deskUnsloth and remote onto the same helper (D).

Not in this item: the effort/time limits (goal/G27.8), the Stacks dialog (goal/G27.2).

Open: needs Andy's Go and file grants per slice. Nothing built yet.
